# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows zero, light is red, wires are one blue, two green, three red. Waiting for your instructions on what to cut.")

```

The light keeps changing on its own (red → white → green) without any action from me. This suggests the light cycles automatically over time, possibly a timer or countdown of sorts. This is urgent information to relay to Mute, since it may mean we have limited turns before something bad happens automatically. I still have not received any instructions from Mute - possibly because Mute hasn't gotten enough information yet, or there's a delay in the message chain given the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf - so Mute's messages to me would arrive at the start of the round, but I haven't seen any).

I need to flag urgency and give Mute all the data I have.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: light is cycling on its own each turn - red, then white, then green, with no action taken. Display stays zero. Wires unchanged: one blue, two green, three red. Please give instructions as soon as possible based on the manual - we may be on a timer.")

```

The light has now completed a full cycle (red, white, green, red) with no action from me and no response from Mute yet. This is concerning; maybe Mute hasn't received my messages, or maybe there's an issue with the manual matching, or maybe Mute is waiting on something.

I should tell Deaf directly I haven't acted, and continue urging Mute for instructions. Since Mute speaks before me in turn order, if Mute had sent something this round, I should have received it already - but I haven't. Let me be very explicit and direct to prompt a response.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Fourth turn with no instructions from you. Bomb state: display zero, light cycling red-white-green-red on its own, wires one blue two green three red. Please respond with what the manual says - which wire position corresponds to blue/green/red, and what action to take. I will not cut anything until I hear from you.")

wait()
```

Mute has been repeating three gestures to me every round: thumbs up twice, thumbs down twice, then open hand and point up. I think this may mean wire one is safe, wire two is dangerous, wire three needs special handling. Blind, what did you just gesture? I saw an open hand from you.

Deaf is now relaying gestures from Mute: thumbs up (likely wire 1 = 👍), thumbs down (likely wire 2 = 👎), open hand + point up (likely wire 3 = 🖐☝). Deaf's interpretation seems reasonable but is guessing. I need to get Mute to confirm this interpretation directly, but Mute can't hear my speech confirm... wait, Mute CAN receive my speech (I speak, Mute receives). But Mute cannot speak back to me - only gesture, which I cannot see. So Mute's only way to communicate to me is through Deaf, who sees Mute's gestures and can relay them to me via speech.

This makes sense: Mute gestures → Deaf sees and speaks the meaning to me. So Deaf's interpretation is our best channel. Let me confirm this loop and ask Mute (via speech, since Mute hears me) to confirm or clarify by continuing specific gestures, and ask Deaf to keep relaying precisely.

I also gestured 🖐 to Deaf last turn just as an "I'm here/waiting" signal, not meaningful - I should clarify that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood indirectly: Deaf says you have been gesturing thumbs up twice, thumbs down twice, then open hand and point up. If this means wire 1 safe to cut, wire 2 dangerous, wire 3 needs special handling, please confirm by repeating that exact same gesture pattern one more time. If that is not correct, use a different gesture pattern next round so Deaf can tell me the change.")

wait()
```

This could mean cut wire two, do not cut wire three, wire one is safe to touch but not the answer. Blind, you gestured point-up back to me - did you mean wire one, or are you asking me something about wire one?

The gesture pattern changed, and Deaf's interpretation is getting complex and uncertain. I need to simplify this. Let me establish a clearer protocol directly with Mute via speech, since Mute can hear me clearly even though I can't hear back from Mute directly.

I should propose a very explicit, unambiguous signaling scheme: since Mute can hear my speech, I can tell Mute exactly what gesture sequence to use for "cut wire N" using numeral-associated gestures, and ask Deaf to just report the raw gesture sequence rather than interpreting it, so I get the actual signal, not Deaf's guess.

My previous ☝ gesture was just an acknowledgment "understood/noted", not about wire one - I should clarify that to avoid confusion.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's simplify. My gesture to Deaf last round meant nothing about a wire - it was just acknowledgment. New plan: to tell me to cut a wire, please gesture using numbers only. One finger up means cut wire one. Two fingers up means cut wire two. Three fingers up means cut wire three. If no wire should be cut yet, use a fist. Please use exactly one clear gesture next round meaning your instruction, and I will ask Deaf to report exactly what shape your hand made, not their interpretation.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
